It says the feature keeps 'all six platform elements (P-1 to P-6): the topology, runtimes, repository roles, the JSON contract rule, the compatibility rule and the security boundary'. But section 1 defines P-6 as 'Named public functions per repository', not a security boundary, and the security/tenancy boundary is only a K-7 check. T-4 treats a provider or model change 'for example through PROV-ACME-2026-11' as a possible future event. Add this to T-1 or N-4: who owns transport and serialisation (TQ-3) may involve the AP API, which is named only in the platform baseline.
